newsitem.title: CHILE: Los Pelambres to seek loans for 70 pct of project.
newsitem.headline: Los Pelambres to seek loans for 70 pct of project.

text.p: Antofagasta Holdings' expects about 70 percent of financing for its massive Los Pelambres copper project to come from a yet-to-be-negotiated syndicated bank loan, a top official said.

The project, due to produce some 260,000 tonnes of copper in concentrates a year by 1999, plans to start a roadshow before serious talks begin toward assembling the loan which could be finished ''within several months,'' he said.

''We've spoken to a number of banks that have registered their interest, but we're at an early stage and we're not in a position to form a syndicate yet,'' said the official, asking not to be identified.
''It's going ahead on track,'' he said.

The remaining 30 percent of the project's $1.3 billion pricetag will come from its partners, London-listed Antofagasta Holdings and two Japanese consortia, in accordance with each one's share in the project, he said.
The $1.3 billion figure includes ''absolutely everything,'' said the offficial, including all construction costs and interest payments while building is proceeding.

Antofagasta signed early this month a letter of intent to sell a combined 40 percent of the mine's equity to a consortium of Nippon Mining & Metals Co Ltd, Marubeni Corp and Mitsui & Co Ltd and another consortium of Mitsubishi Corp and Mitsubishi Materials Corp.
Antofagasta holds the majority 60 percent share and has no current plans to sell more, company officials have said.

Financing details are a long way off but Los Pelambres is confident the size of its reserves, mineable ore of 930 million tonnes at an average grade of 0.75 percent, and Chile's low country risk will allow it to win good terms, said the official.
''We expect to win project financing that's absolutely competitive with any project in the world.
We don't expect to pay over the odds for financing, with the reserves we have,'' he said.

Chile's ambassador in Tokyo, Jaime Lagos Erazo, said the Japanese partners would put up a combined $400 million to $500 million corresponding to their 40 percent share and that their buy-in reflected Chile's low country risk.

The project, in Chile's Fourth Region east of the town of Illapel near the Argentine border, will come onstream at roughly the same time as two other major new copper mines, Collahuasi and Codelco's Radomiro Tomic, and during major expansion at Escondida.
